record.paper_title: Developments and open problems on chiral polytopes
record.original_question: Does every orientably regular polytope admit an infinite chiral extension?

evidence.quote: Problem 29 Does every orientably regular polytope admit an infinite chiral extension?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An abstract polytope is a ranked partially ordered set satisfying the standard axioms generalizing the face lattices of convex polytopes (existence of greatest and least elements, the diamond condition on intervals of length 2, and strong flag-connectedness). For an abstract n-polytope P, its automorphism group Γ(P) acts on the flags of P. The polytope P is called regular if Γ(P) is transitive on flags. If P is regular, its rotation subgroup (the subgroup generated by the products of consecutive standard generating reflections) has index 1 or 2 in Γ(P); when the index equals 2, P is called orientably regular. The polytope P is called chiral if Γ(P) has exactly two orbits on flags, with adjacent flags lying in different orbits.

Given an abstract n-polytope K, a chiral extension of K is a chiral (n+1)-polytope all of whose facets are isomorphic to K.

Question: Does every orientably regular abstract polytope K admit a chiral extension that has infinitely many faces (i.e., an infinite chiral extension)?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature (Cunningham–Pellicer, Montero, and others through 2021–2024) establishes finite chiral extensions for finite chiral polytopes with regular facets and constructs infinite chiral extensions in special cases, but no source found resolves the general question of whether every orientably regular polytope admits an infinite chiral extension. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Chiral extensions of chiral polytopes (Cunningham–Pellicer)
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of chiral extensions whose facets are given chiral polytopes with regular facets.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes existence of (finite or infinite) chiral extensions in particular cases but does not settle the general question for all orientably regular polytopes.

status_evidence.title: On the Schläfli symbol of chiral extensions of polytopes (Montero)
status_evidence.snippet: Constructions controlling Schläfli symbols of chiral extensions.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress on chiral extensions; general infinite-extension problem not resolved.

status_evidence.title: Developments and open problems on chiral polytopes
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing the problem on infinite chiral extensions as open.
